renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: simpleaf_barcode_rank_knee
  title: Barcode rank plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a barcode ranked by its UMI count, from the richest droplet down, on log axes, with one curve per sample. It answers where real cells stop and empty droplets start.
    How to read: a good library has a plateau of cells with high counts, a steep drop and a long flat tail of ambient barcodes. A curve with no clear drop, or one where the called cells sit on the tail, points to a noisy or low-quality library. Compare it with the Cell Ranger curve of the same sample.
    Lines and annotations: the marked cut-off is where the called cells end. alevin-fry reports every barcode it quantified and calls no cells itself, so the cells are CellBender's cell-barcode list for this sample and the line is a data-defined reference, not a threshold from the tool.
  kind: knee_plot
  roles:
    sample: sample
    rank: rank
    umi_count: umi_count
    is_cell: is_cell

- component: card
  title: UMI count per barcode
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest UMI count of any barcode, with the total UMIs beside it, and the histogram shows how counts are distributed over barcodes. It answers how deep the richest droplets are and how skewed the library is.
    How to read: a few barcodes with very high counts and a long tail of near-empty ones is the normal shape of droplet data. Use the knee plot to see where the cells end.
  column: umi_count
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - sum
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: UMI counts, per barcode

- component: table
  title: Barcodes by rank
  description: |-
    Each row is a barcode with its rank, UMI count and whether it is in the called cell list. It answers which barcodes carry the library.
    How to read: sort by rank to see the richest barcodes and check that the called cells are the top ones.

- component: card
  title: Mapping rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of reads that piscem mapped, with the lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how well the reads fit the reference index.
    How to read: a sample far below the others points to a wrong reference, a poor library or contamination. The tool publishes no pass mark for this rate, so compare samples with each other.
  column: mapping_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: lowest and highest sample
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Reads processed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of reads processed across samples, and the box shows the spread per sample. It answers how much sequencing each sample received and how even it was.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer reads than the others may give fewer cells or a noisier profile.
  column: num_processed
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: reads per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Cells quantified
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of barcodes alevin-fry quantified as cells across samples, and the box shows the spread per sample. It answers how many cells each sample yields.
    How to read: compare with the number of cells loaded. A sample with a very different count from its replicates may have a calling or capture problem.
  column: num_cells
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: cells per sample, with their spread

- component: table
  title: Mapping summary per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with its reads processed, reads mapped, mapping rate and number of cells. It answers how each sample performed at mapping and cell calling.
    How to read: sort by mapping rate to find the weakest sample first.
